meta.note: The roster source of truth and the only home of a skill number. engine/skills.ts is the one calculator and the client calls the same function, so a press is never typed twice. tools/skills.ts --calc prints the workshop; --checks runs the mechanic gate.

type_meta.attack: Order list · cooldown + Mana or current-HP cost
type_meta.buff: Timed self-buff - own cd and duration, never persists between fights
type_meta.curse: Attached to target · Uses same hit_chance as attacks

reservation.note: The player opens auras; the only system rule is that total reserved mana may not reach 100% of the pool — some mana must stay usable for skills. There is no other cap.

cast_conditions.note: The cast order's condition list, held per conditional slot rather than shared, so two rows may wait on different facts. A row fires while any one of its legs holds, so a list is an OR and the player never writes an expression. The legs: `boss` (the front target is a boss), `hpBelowPct` (our own pool is under that share), `statusMissing` (the target lacks a status or curse this row applies), `minTargets` (the group is at least that wide) and `manaFloorPct` (the press must leave that share of the usable pool). Each `*_default` is the number a leg opens at when its tick-box is first checked and the player edits it from there; they are the only defaults any screen may show, so no screen types its own.

ladder.note: The duplicate ladder (skill-pool-system.md 'Duplicates -> ladder'): each step buys a share of cooldown reduction and costs duplicates of its own. `step` is the rung, `cdr` the percent it buys, `cost` the duplicates it takes; `duplicatesToStep` is the running sum of the costs, so the top of the ladder costs what the whole ladder costs. engine/skills.ts reads this table - the ladder a duplicate climbs is one home, and the wiki prints the same rows.

formula.note: press = (base_flat + (eff/100) x power + (max_hp_pct/100) x caster Max HP) x (1 + (skill_level - 1) x level_step_pct/100) - the PoE shape: `base_flat` is the skill own damage at skill level 1 (its identity, the same for every caster), `eff` is the share of the added power line the press receives, so gear scales a row by its effectiveness instead of by a percentage of the finished hit. power = the row basis - phys = the caster finished physical hit, magic = their magic + Element x Alignment/100 (B5). `archetype_bands` is the calibration the pairs were derived from: a row damage per second is set by its archetype and the pinned maximum is the roster own best cooldown row per basis, so the DPS line read back out of the curve does not move while a press reads as a heavy or a light hit. Read by engine/skills.ts `perPress` - the --calc workshop, the attack-table press column and the client casts all call it, so a press is never computed twice. A paid active row uses exactly one typed flat price: `mana: N flat` or `hp_cost: N flat`. Both climb on `mana_level_step_pct`; HP is paid from the caster's current pool and leaves one point, while only Mana receives the configured AoE premium. Neither pool size changes a flat price. Mana rows were priced against the level-1 caster's own pool, derived from `level_gain.mana_base` and `stat.base` on `K.K_INT_MP`; it is a pricing reference, never a term of the formula.

archetype_bands.note: Provenance, not a formula: these are the bands the roster's press pairs were derived from — a slow single-target nuke sits at the top of its power line, an area row pays a penalty for the targets it reaches, a fast filler sits below — and each row's per-press is that rate inverted, so a press reads as a heavy or a light hit instead of every row pressing the same. `base_share` is how much of the press is the row's own flat (a nuke) versus its effectiveness on the caster power line (a filler). The pinned maximum is the roster's own best cooldown row per basis, so the DPS line the curve prices does not move. **No formula reads this block and no gate checks it**: the derived numbers live in each row's own `base_flat` / `eff` / cooldown, which is what `perPress` actually spends, so editing a band here changes nothing in the game and the block exists only to record how the pairs were chosen. The cooldown-less beat row keeps its own press.

skill_levels.note: One row per skill level: the multiplier a press and an effect carry at that level. `damage_pct` is the ramp the roster always had; `effect_pct` is the lever that used to be absent (a value in a row is its level-1 number, and it climbs with this column). `special_level_effects` lists the effect stats that opt out of the ramp: Energy Absorb interpolates its base toward its cap across the level range, and Ghost Dance counts a charge every N levels, so both already spend skill level and must not be scaled twice. Row 1 is the FLOOR a fresh skill starts on, not the finished value: a skill dropped at level 1 presses a quarter of what it will, and grows into its press as it levels. `buff_effect_pct` is the buff/aura lever: those rows open at their whole stored value — a dropped buff or aura is usable the moment it lands — and climb to a higher cap than every other effect rides, whole numbers only so a printed rung reads as a percentage and never a fraction.
